candidate.title: Google OAuth refresh persists unvalidated credential.key (schema validation bypass) in credential-sharing mode
candidate.file: unknown (not in PR diff); search in Google OAuth refresh/credential update code for `parseRefreshTokenResponse(` and `credential.update({ data: { key: ... } })`
reports: [advisory] google's refresh now persists parserefreshtokenresponse(googlecredentials, ...) instead of schema.parse(googlecredentials) on the pre-existing credential object, so under credential-sharing mode the loose minimum schema replaces the strict googlecredentialschema validation of the entire stored key. in sharing mode, arbitrary/unvalidated fields from the mutated googlecredentials object (and, once the bogus-computed-key bug is fixed, from any remote response field) are written into credential.key without googlecredentialschema checking — malformed keys get persisted permanently, and readers of credential.key that assume the google shape (e.g. expirydate typing) read misinterpreted data.
